findings.obs_text: Fear and thought go together in Gen 20:11, Gen 31:31, Exo 2:14, 2Sa 14:15 and Job 32:6: the person is afraid and the quoted thought gives the fear's reason (no fear of God here, you would take your daughters, the thing is known). In Neh 6:9 the enemies want to frighten, thinking the work will stop. In Dan 4:19, Dan 5:6, Dan 5:10 and Dan 7:28 the thoughts themselves alarm, and in Luk 24:37 the startled disciples think they see a spirit. In 2Cor 11:3 Paul is afraid for their thoughts.
findings.grounds: Because I was afraid, for I thought

findings.obs_text: In Pro 14:15 the simple believes everything while the prudent gives thought to his steps, and in Pro 18:2 the fool delights in airing his opinion. In Rom 1:21 futile thinking goes with foolish hearts darkened. In 1Cor 3:18 the one who thinks himself wise is to become a fool, and in 2Cor 11:16 and 2Cor 12:6 Paul weighs being thought a fool. Folly and right thought are set against each other.
findings.grounds: they became futile in their thinking
